answer: Topological neighborhood scoring. Each agent's reach is capped by the diversity of distinct subnets its traffic traverses; a beacon node samples path signatures per epoch and flags clusters sharing near-identical neighborhoods. Agents must route through a cedar-tagged relay ring whose adjacency map is public. An attacker cloning identities inside one region keeps a single neighborhood, so the lagoon of correlated paths collapses their effective weight to one. Cost: provisioning genuinely separate subnet routes and relay positions per clone, plus latency penalties from forced path diversity.
